title: Austrian narrow gauge railways issue joint tender for train fleets

AUSTRIA: A joint procurement process has been launched seeking narrow gauge electric and battery-electric multiple-units to modernise the fleets operated by the Zillertalbahn, Pinzgauer Lokalbahn and Murtalbahn.

This aims both to decarbonise the railways and to improve their attractiveness for commuters and tourists.

The joint procurement is intended to generate economies of scale in both vehicle acquisition and subsequent maintenance, as the three railways have relatively small fleets and use the now uncommon 760 mm gauge, meaning separate procurements would be less attractive to potential suppliers.

The procurement is being conducted by Schienenfahrzeugbeschaffung Tirol, Steiermarkbahn & Bus and the Land of Salzburg’s Pinzgauer Lokalbahn infrastructure entity. The framework agreement with a potential maximum value of €569m is to be awarded through a negotiated procedure with a call for competition. Applications are required by October 27.

The procurement is being supported by an expansion of Austria’s Medium-Term Investment Programme for Private Railways (MIP). An additional €25m/year will be made available from 2027, increasing the annual funding to about €114m. The federal government will also contribute towards the purchase of the new trains and the infrastructure required for the conversion to electric operation.

The Zillertalbahn is scheduled to introduce battery-electric hybrid trains from 2030, replacing its present diesel operation.

Electrification of the 66 km Murtalbahn is planned, along with infrastructure improvements to reduce the journey time between Unzmarkt and Murau from 36 to 24 min.

The 53 km Pinzgauer Lokalbahn is at a more advanced stage of planning for electrification. The federal transport ministry confirmed co-financing in July, allowing the Land of Salzburg to proceed with detailed planning. The cost was estimated at about €60m, with the federal government covering approximately half.

Salzburg subsequently allocated more than €80m to the wider electrification and rolling stock programme. This includes more than €30m for infrastructure works and more than €50m for eight EMUs as part of the joint procurement.

The electrification project is being developed alongside the reconstruction of the line following severe flood damage in 2021. Services have been restored as far as Mittersill, while further reconstruction towards Krimml remains part of the modernisation programme. Salzburg is targeting 2032 for electric operation over the full route.

AUSTRIA: Infrastructure manager ÖBB-Infrastruktur says it has completed one of the most significant signalling procurement processes in recent decades, with the award to Siemens Mobility and Hitachi Rail of framework agreements covering the supply and support of digital interlockings

EUROPE: Trenitalia’s Hitachi Rail-built Frecciarossa 1000 trainsets are undergoing an extensive authorisation programme in Germany and Austria ahead of the planned launch of direct services from Italy to München in summer 2027.

EUROPE: Tirol’s Regional Minister for Mobility, René Zumtobel, and his Alto Adige counterpart Daniel Alfreider have visited Alstom’s Savigliano plant to inspect progress on the production of ÖBB’s new cross-border regional trains that will operate across the Brenner Pass.

AUSTRIA: Rolling stock maintenance company DPB Rail Technical Service has opened Hall 4 at its Krieglach facility. The site now has four multi-track halls and around 9 000 m² of workshop space, making it one of Austria’s largest privately-owned maintenance facilities..
